_about: SoundEdit's tool definitions, as SoundEdit 1.2.3's own MCP server lists them. Read only by glama/stand-in.js for Glama's build check.
instructions: SoundEdit is a sample editor the person is watching and listening to while you work; it also runs headless, with no window. Times are in seconds unless an argument names another unit. Every position read back also gives its frame at the document's sample rate, named with it: frames are zero-based, one frame across all channels, and a range's end is exclusive (a..<b holds frames a through b − 1). For an exact selection use start_frame/end_frame; a reply gives what changed in frames. Every edit lands in the file's History and can be undone (edit · edit.undo); nothing is written over the person's file. Read the state first; select a range before a range edit. The Library tools (library_*, recipe_*, deliver_*) work on a folder of sounds: open it, query it with the Library's filter words, stage a recipe and preview a row before anything is made; override a row that is wrong; then run it. A card's "unsure" marks a guess SoundEdit could not confirm by ear: keep it out of names, tags and INFO, tell the person which sounds it could not identify, and give their answer to library_teach. A tool that writes files goes ahead and shows in SoundEdit's band, or waits for the person's Return there if they asked SoundEdit to wait. Headless calls require prior folder access and write permission; they refuse instead of opening a panel.

tools.name: get_state
tools.description: The open file: its name and path, length, rate, channels and which of them are lit (what edits, the selection and playback are on), the selection, markers, slices, whether it plays, and what History can undo. Its length and every position count the file's own frames, at the rate named beside them: the file's own, whatever rate the audio device runs at.

tools.description: Select using start/end in seconds, start_frame/end_frame for exact sample frames, or all for the whole file. Use only one form. The end is exclusive; leaving it out places a caret. tools.name: library_open
tools.description: Open a folder of sounds in SoundEdit's Library — every file named at once, measured as the walk goes — or open one file in the editor.
tools.title: Open in Library
Query the Library
tools.name: library_query
tools.description: Narrow the open folder's rows by the Library's filter words, or by plain words ("short punchy kick", "quiet vocal loops at 120") read into those words as the person's Return reads them, the reply saying what ran — the same filter the person sees in the window — and read each sound's card: what it is, how sure and what else it might be; four words for how long, bright, noisy and pitched it is; its length, format, level, loudness, root, key, tempo, shape and History. With like, the rows that sound most like one file come first. What the card calls unsure is a guess SoundEdit could not confirm: never put it in a name, a tag or INFO — leave it out and ask the person, and give their answer to library_teach.

filter.description: the Library's filter words, ANDed: a bare word matches the name; is kick, tempo 80-110, lufs >-14, len <1s, note C, key Am (or key A minor, key 8A, key A, key minor), peak >-1, clip >0, stereo, mono, loop, history, ext wav, tag drums, hits >4, form perc. Empty: every row

wait_seconds.description: seconds to wait for the facts still being measured (default 10)

brief.description: one line a sound instead of the card

offset.description: cards to skip, to page through (default 0)

tools.title: Split a session
Facts of files
tools.description: Measure sound files named by path and read each one's card — what it is, how sure and what else it might be; four words for how long, bright, noisy and pitched it is; its length, format, level, loudness, root, key, tempo, shape and History — as the Library measures them, without opening their folder. For a whole folder, library_open and library_query.

tools.description: Run the staged recipe, as the person's ⌘⏎: a recipe that writes files writes them and leaves each source and its History as they were; one that writes nothing puts its steps in each staged file's own History — undoable, the source never touched. A row whose History already holds this recipe's run, or that was edited by hand, takes no step again and writes its outputs from it. A step a Library run doesn't take is refused, by name, before anything is asked. It waits for the person's Return in the Library only if they asked SoundEdit to wait.

tools.title: Library
tools.name: library
library_command
tools.title: Library field
tools.description: Run the words the person types in the Library's field, on the rows given (or selected). `rename {is} {n}` renames the files in place by their measured word and a number (tokens: {name} {is} {n} {tempo} {key} {note} …; {is} leaves an unsure class out); `names` renames them to the agent's own names, which leave out an instrument or key the card calls unsure, as {is} does (refused otherwise, unless person_said); `write` writes their tempo, root, loop and tags into the files' own chunks (Write Into Files); `group drums`, `ungroup`, `smart kicks` keep Groups; `lock 98` sets the Library tempo. A rename and Write Into Files show in the band (and wait for the person's Return there if they asked SoundEdit to wait); each undoes with library.undo.

names.description: a rename the agent wrote itself: one name for each row given or selected, in order

items.description: a new name, without the extension

rows.description: the rows it acts on; leave out for the rows selected now

wait_seconds.description: seconds to wait for the person's Return (default 120)

text.description: what the person types in the Library's field: rename {is} {n} · group drums · ungroup · smart kicks · write · lock 98 · lock folder · sort lufs · columns …

person_said.description: true only when the person told you these instruments or keys themselves

high.description: HIGH, as the person types it in INFO; empty: the measured value back

key.description: KEY, as the person types it in INFO; empty: the measured value back

root.description: ROOT, as the person types it in INFO; empty: the measured value back

beats.description: BEATS, as the person types it in INFO; empty: the measured value back

rows.description: the rows it acts on; leave out for the rows selected now

person_said.description: true only when the person told you these instruments or keys themselves

tools.description: Set INFO's fields on the rows given (or selected), as the person types them: tempo (98, 8 beats, 2 bars, x2, none), key (Am), root (C3), low, high, velocity, loop, meter, title, artist, comment, copyright, date, finder (Finder's tags). Kept with each sound; library_command `write` puts them into the files. Undoes with library.undo. A class is the person's to correct: library_teach. A key on a row whose card is unsure of it is the person's to give (person_said).

Library files
tools.name: library_files
tools.description: Copy or move the rows' files (given or selected) into a folder, Copy as Heard (as the Library plays them: LOCK's tempo, KEY's key, their History) into one, or move them to the Trash — never a hard delete. Shows in the band (waiting for the person's Return if they asked SoundEdit to wait); undoes with library.undo.

folder.description: the folder to copy, move or copy as heard into (made if it is not there); ~ is home

rows.description: the rows it acts on; leave out for the rows selected now

action.description: what to do with the rows' files

wait_seconds.description: seconds to wait for the person's Return (default 120)

tools.name: file
tools.title: Save or export

wait_seconds.description: seconds to wait for the person's Return (default 120)

path.description: save_as: the new file's path (.wav, .aif, .caf, .flac); the exports: the folder to make their folder in; ~ is home

tools.description: Write the open file, as the person's File menu: save (Save Edit: the edit as a file of its own, the source untouched), save_as (to a path; its extension the container, the document's own rate, depth and channels), export_slices or export_marker_regions (a folder of files in the folder named), export_channels (a mono file for each lit channel, in a folder made in the folder named). Waits for the person's Return in the Library's band only if they asked SoundEdit to wait; the reply says where it went.

tools.title: Ask for Pro
tools.name: pro_trial
tools.description: When a tool answers that it is SoundEdit Pro, ask the person for it: SoundEdit comes forward and the Library's band asks them — a click on its Pro line starts Pro's 14-day trial, or, the trial used, the purchase card is up. The agent never starts the trial or buys; this waits for the person and says whether Pro is on.

wait_seconds.description: seconds to wait for the person (default 60)
